question: On 400-node three-hour churn with mixed 60s, 300s and 15s samples, do RAW_UUID native TimeSeries read gains from single-sample Jenkins persist, or does LowCardinality(UUID) regain CPU/storage value?
baseline: unmodified stock O1 ClickHouse LLVM22 41596421285, binary SHA256 f0a2fa1f814c58853f43423705cac10ab9df3bfe5887e27ebe9620ba7cb9660e
candidate: RAW_UUID tuple inner ID on TAGS, SAMPLES, TimeRanges; identical hash expression and tags index, same executable and synthetic rows
fixture: Deterministic generator, 400 active node slots, 3h life; one 60s node series, two 300s pod series and 1% 15s burst pod series each lifetime; 3d initial. SHA and distribution manifest from generation; no real customer data
single_variable: Tuple(UInt64,LowCardinality(UUID)) versus Tuple(UInt64,UUID) across all TimeSeries inner ID columns, same source/LLVM/flags/query/data
math_bound: A 3h life yields 180 points at 60s, 36 at 300s and 720 at 15s, unlike single-point Jenkins. LC incurs O(D) dictionary hashing/zeroing, but saves approx (16-2)*N UUID bytes when many samples reuse one ID; RAW may win CPU but lose compression for dense series; measured test must decide.
falsifier: Full native PromQL labels/timestamps/value mismatch; invalid ID digest, wrong fixture counts/hash; drift >25%; RAW CPU wall p95 or RSS/parts regress on repeated-ID selections, or query OOM; keep negative outcome.
test_matrix: 400 slots x 8 3h lifetimes/day x3d; metric node 60s, pod 5min and 1% 15s; native avg_over_time selector exact project/namespace/pod/whole at day/3d windows; first isolated single runner 2 warmups+4 runs A/B/B/A; no code compilation; 14d/clients only if memory/correctness gates pass.
runner_budget: One ubuntu-24.04 4-vCPU benchmark job <=90m, 1 concurrent run; 3d synthetic data 2-3m samples, with memory and physical-part ceilings; use cached stock O1 binary, no recompile.
planned_workflow: .github/workflows/ts-lab-r01-k8s-mixed-20261103.yml self-path-only push and workflow_dispatch, unique run_id group; separate cheap fixture unit CI
